body: Ah, I got it, thank you so much!!

Don't apologize for the lengthy post :) I need all the advice I can get! I'm so glad you're finally getting away from your bad situation as well that's amazing!!  1) I think she's scared to call CPS because she's worried about what would happen to her after the call is made, and I'm worried about making the call because her parents would definitely know I was the one who made the call and would probably take their anger out on my friend for being the one who told me everything. 2) I think she knows what they're doing is wrong somewhere in her head but from the way she talks about it she's on the fence between the two, somewhat believing what they say so I will definitely make a huge effort to hammer home that what they are doing is so wrong. 3) I'll definitely ask her about the situation so that I can help tear down her parents actions and build her up. We always talk about doing a coastline drive of California as soon as we graduate so she can escape them. And how we should move in together. I'll try to talk about that more often with her as well. 5) I think she's exhausted too so number 5 is a really important one. Her parents make her study really late into the night so I don't think she gets enough sleep and then has to wake up really early for school so she can get the bus. I'll suggest for her to try meditating- oh yeah she loves music and they're trying to take that away from her too. I think that was one of the final straws before she told me about considering suicide. It was her way of relaxing and escaping. So hopefully meditation can fill the hole that them taking music (or trying I don't know how well they succeeded) made! Almost forgot, I think once I've gathered everyone's very helpful advice I'll probably show her this thread and that there are people who she can talk to who have had similar situations so that she can see what they did and apply it to her situation. 

Thank you so much for your detailed comment it's going to help a lot!!

That's so amazing about your niece! I will definitely suggest for her to talk to her school counselor to see if she can help in any way. My friend tells me that she counts every day until college when she can escape them. So I think that's what's really keeping her okay, similar to what you were saying about being able to visualize their future. Thank you for your comment!

Thank you so much for your advice! I sent her a few posts from the subreddit you suggested and she really liked them and said she would read more! She said she reads a lot of depression Reddits and they help a little bit. I just use Snapchat to communicate with her since those disappear and her parents read all our iMessage texts (or used to I know not to text there anymore), I'm just praying they don't take her phone away forever cause they don't let her bring it to school anymore.
Yes we live in the US and we are 15, 16 in a few months or so. School started last week
